Lameness
• Refers to the inability to properly use one or more limbs.
• One of the most economic problems in dairying.
Causes:
1. Infectious – causes by bacteria specially Fusobacterium necrophorum.
2. Nutritional – foot rot is common in zinc, selenium and copper deficient cows.
3. Injuries – sharp objects such as stones or hardware may penetrate the hoof wall that may lead to entry of pathogens that may result to infection.
4. Genetics – some breed are prone to hoof problems

facts: Lameness refers to the inability of a cow to properly use one or more limbs.
Lameness is one of the most significant economic problems in dairy farming.
Infectious lameness is caused by bacteria, especially Fusobacterium necrophorum.
Nutritional lameness and foot rot are common in cows deficient in zinc, selenium, and copper.
Injuries from sharp objects such as stones or hardware can penetrate the hoof wall, allowing pathogens to enter and cause infection.
Genetics can cause lameness as some cattle breeds are predisposed or prone to hoof problems.
Bovine foot anatomy includes the medial claw, lateral claw, interdigital space/claw, and accessory digits (dewclaws).
Structures of the bovine claw include the bulb of heel, sole, white line, axial wall, abaxial wall, and outer wall.
